paragraphs: Concept bottleneck models make predictions through an intermediate set of high-level concepts. Their usefulness therefore depends on which concepts are available, yet the paper argues that the properties of a good concept set have not been clearly understood. It develops a theoretical account of concepts organized around expressiveness and model-aware inductive bias, while making the underlying assumption of these models explicit.

The theory connects these properties to predictive performance. In appropriate regimes, a well-designed concept set can reduce the amount of training data needed and improve robustness when the data distribution changes. These are conditional benefits of suitable concept choices, rather than a claim that introducing a concept bottleneck always improves a model.

The authors turn these insights into a method for selecting informative concepts that avoid redundancy. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and MetaShift show improvements over the foundational embedding counterpart, especially with little training data and under distribution shifts. The paper also examines failure modes, making concept selection itself a central part of designing effective models.
neurips-2024-a-theoretical-design-of-con.tldr: A theory of concept-set design guides concept selection that can improve data efficiency and robustness in suitable regimes.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to make gradient descent and the proximal gradient method adapt their step sizes to the function being optimized. The central idea is to use local curvature information: how the gradient changes around the points the algorithm encounters. This makes the observed behavior of the objective part of the rule for choosing subsequent steps.

The proposed versions obtain that information from differences between observed gradients. According to the abstract, doing so adds no computational cost. The contribution is therefore an adaptive update rule for two fundamental first-order methods, using information available during optimization to guide how far each update moves.

The authors prove convergence under the assumption that the gradient is locally Lipschitz, which constrains how rapidly it changes locally. Their versions also permit larger step sizes than those suggested in the earlier method they reference. The stated result combines adaptivity and a convergence guarantee under that local regularity assumption; it does not establish that larger permitted steps necessarily produce faster optimization in every problem.
neurips-2024-adaptive-proximal-gradient-.tldr: Adaptive gradient methods use observed gradient differences to permit larger steps while retaining convergence under local Lipschitz assumptions.

paragraphs: Speech recognition systems must align information in an audio sequence with the text they produce. In the systems discussed here, this alignment is ordinarily handled during decoding. The paper finds that a transformer encoder can instead align the information internally during its forward pass, before the decoder starts producing text.

That observation motivates the Aligner-Encoder. Training uses frame-wise cross-entropy rather than the dynamic programming used by RNN-Transducer. The decoder retains lightweight recurrence over text but removes learned cross-attention. It reads embedding frames in order and produces one token per frame until it predicts the end of the message. Internal alignment makes this simpler decoding process possible.

Experiments report performance close to the state of the art, including a configuration for long-form speech recognition. In one representative comparison, total inference is twice as fast as RNN-T and sixteen times as fast as AED. The authors also observe clear audio-text alignment in one layer’s self-attention weights, connecting the efficiency result to a visible internal behavior.
neurips-2024-aligner-encoders-self-atten.tldr: Transformer encoders can align audio with text internally, enabling simpler speech recognition with faster inference in a representative comparison.

paragraphs: Time series domain adaptation transfers knowledge from labeled source data to an unlabeled target domain. The paper focuses on two qualities a useful representation needs: distinguishing examples within a domain and transferring across domains. Its motivating finding is that frequency features are more discriminative within a domain, while temporal features transfer better across domains.

Adversarial Co-learning Networks, or ACON, organize learning around these complementary strengths. A frequency component captures multiple periodic patterns. Mutual learning between temporal and frequency representations improves the source-domain discriminability of temporal features and the target-domain transferability of frequency features. Each representation helps strengthen the property that is less developed in the other.

ACON also performs domain adversarial learning in subspaces describing correlations between temporal and frequency features, rather than in their original feature spaces. This further targets transferability for both representations. Experiments across numerous time series datasets and five applications report state-of-the-art performance, supporting the value of coordinating the two feature types according to their different strengths.
neurips-2024-boosting-transferability-an.tldr: ACON coordinates temporal and frequency features to improve both cross-domain transfer and discrimination in time series.

paragraphs: ConvBench evaluates large vision-language models through conversations that continue across multiple turns. It contains 577 curated conversations covering 215 broad, open-ended tasks intended to resemble real user behavior. The goal is to assess visual assistants in an interaction setting where several different capabilities contribute to a response.

Within each conversation, the benchmark progressively examines perception, reasoning, and creativity. Its evaluation can separate these capabilities, helping attribute an error to the ability responsible for it. This matters because a model’s performance on a reasoning or creative task can also depend on whether it correctly perceived the visual input. The paper additionally introduces automatic evaluation for the varied open-ended questions.

The reported experiments find substantial difficulty for the evaluated models: GPT4V receives a score of 39.51%. The authors also find that weak perception inhibits models’ reasoning and creative strengths. ConvBench therefore contributes both a demanding conversation benchmark and a way to diagnose how failures in one capability affect performance elsewhere.
neurips-2024-convbench-a-multi-turn-conv.tldr: ConvBench evaluates multi-turn visual conversations while separating perception, reasoning, and creativity to identify sources of failure.

paragraphs: CoVoMix addresses speech generation for conversations involving several speakers and multiple rounds of dialogue. The paper starts from the observation that progress in high-quality text-to-speech has not fully resolved conversational naturalness. A conversation includes interactions between voices, and generating fluent individual utterances does not by itself capture those interactions.

The model first converts dialogue text into separate streams of discrete tokens carrying semantic information for each talker. A flow-matching acoustic model then uses these streams to produce mixed mel-spectrograms, which represent the combined audio. Finally, a HiFi-GAN model converts that representation into speech waveforms. This pipeline explicitly carries multiple speakers’ information into the acoustic generation stage.

The authors also introduce metrics for evaluating dialogue modeling and generation. Their experiments demonstrate natural and coherent multi-round conversations with multiple talkers. Examples include a single audio channel combining one person’s utterance with another’s laughter or interjections. Such outputs illustrate the model’s ability to generate listener participation alongside the main speaker’s speech.
neurips-2024-covomix-advancing-zero-shot.tldr: CoVoMix generates multi-speaker conversations with overlapping speech, interjections, and laughter through a coordinated token-to-audio pipeline.

paragraphs: DetectRL examines whether methods for identifying LLM-generated text remain reliable under conditions resembling real use. Strong detection results in existing evaluations leave this question unresolved. The authors build a benchmark from human-written material in domains where LLM misuse is a concern, alongside text generated by popular language models.

The benchmark includes generated text altered through heuristic rules. These changes simulate advanced prompting, human revisions such as word substitutions, and writing errors. Including these variants makes the evaluation sensitive to how text can change between its initial generation and the form a detector eventually receives.

The study analyzes how writing style, generating model, attack method, text length, and aspects of human writing affect different detectors. It reports that even state-of-the-art detection techniques underperform on the benchmark. The contribution is a more stressful evaluation framework that reveals strengths and weaknesses across conditions, rather than a single detection result being treated as evidence of broad real-world reliability.
neurips-2024-detectrl-benchmarking-llm-g.tldr: DetectRL exposes weaknesses in AI-text detectors using generated text that simulates realistic prompting, revisions, and writing errors.

paragraphs: Model Predictive Shielding protects a reinforcement learning agent by using a backup policy when its proposed actions are risky. Such protection can remain active during training and deployment, but conservative backup behavior can impede the task. Dynamic Model Predictive Shielding aims to make recovery actions advance the objective while preserving safety.

DMPS uses a local planner to choose safe recovery actions based on both immediate progress and longer-term rewards. The neural policy helps the planner estimate rewards beyond its short planning horizon. In the other direction, the policy learns from the planner’s recovery plans. This exchange makes safety interventions a source of task-relevant learning.

The paper establishes safety during and after training and bounds recovery regret, with the bound decreasing exponentially as planning depth increases. Experiments find that trained policies rarely need the shield and achieve higher rewards than several state-of-the-art baselines. The theoretical and empirical results address complementary goals: preserving safety guarantees and reducing how much recovery behavior obstructs useful progress.
neurips-2024-dynamic-model-predictive-sh.tldr: DMPS combines local planning and policy learning to choose productive recovery actions while maintaining provable safety.

paragraphs: Evaluating language models as embodied decision makers is difficult when systems use different tasks, inputs, outputs, and responsibilities. A final success rate also hides why an agent failed. Embodied Agent Interface addresses these problems by providing a common way to formalize tasks and the specifications of language-model components.

The interface covers goals about states as well as goals extending over time. It organizes four common model responsibilities: interpreting goals, breaking them into subgoals, sequencing actions, and modeling transitions. This shared structure allows evaluation to focus on particular decision-making functions instead of treating the entire agent as one indivisible system.

Its metrics distinguish error types, including hallucinations, affordance errors, and several planning errors. The resulting benchmark is designed to reveal strengths and weaknesses at the subtask level. This matters for deciding where a language model can contribute effectively within an embodied system, because the same overall failure can arise from very different problems in understanding, planning, or predicting action outcomes.
neurips-2024-embodied-agent-interface-be.tldr: Embodied Agent Interface standardizes embodied decision-making evaluations and breaks failures down by model responsibility and error type.

paragraphs: Many vision-language models accept two-dimensional images, whereas MRI and CT scans typically contain three-dimensional information. This paper approaches that mismatch through data selection. Vote-MI is an unsupervised, one-pass method that chooses representative two-dimensional slices from a three-dimensional scan, providing selected views for use with existing vision-language models.

To study this approach, the authors introduce BrainMD, containing 2,453 annotated three-dimensional brain MRI scans paired with radiology reports and electronic health records. They also build BrainMD-select for representative-slice selection and BrainBench for downstream vision-language tasks. Together, these resources connect the quality of selected views with their usefulness in subsequent tasks.

Experiments on these resources show improved zero-shot and few-shot performance. Compared with randomly selecting examples, Vote-MI produces average absolute gains of 14.6% and 16.6%, respectively. The findings support representative slice selection as a useful way to apply two-dimensional models to this medical imaging setting, with improvements arising from how scan information is presented to the model.
neurips-2024-enhancing-vision-language-m.tldr: Vote-MI selects representative MRI slices to improve two-dimensional vision-language models’ zero-shot and few-shot performance on BrainMD.

paragraphs: Feature-attribution explanations highlight inputs intended to account for a prediction. Evaluations often reward explanations that preserve predictive information. The problem studied here is that some explanations carry extra information beyond what their displayed input values appear to contain, allowing them to achieve deceptively strong prediction-based scores. The paper calls these encoding explanations.

The authors define encoding through conditional dependence and show that this definition captures existing examples. It also characterizes a desirable property of non-encoding explanations: they contain all informative inputs used to produce the explanation. That makes the visible explanation a transparent account of the information involved in constructing it.

The paper proves that ROAR, FRESH, and EVAL-X do not rank non-encoding explanations above encoding ones, then introduces STRIPE-X to obtain the correct ranking. Empirical demonstrations support the theoretical analysis. Applying STRIPE-X to a sentiment-analysis task reveals encoding in LLM-generated explanations even when the model was explicitly prompted to avoid it, showing why instructions alone did not ensure transparency in that setting.
neurips-2024-explanations-that-reveal-al.tldr: A formal definition of explanation encoding leads to STRIPE-X, which distinguishes transparent explanations from those carrying extra predictive information.

paragraphs: Precipitation nowcasting models can perform well on pixel-wise measures while producing blurry forecasts with limited operational usefulness. This paper changes the training objective to address that problem. Fourier Amplitude and Correlation Loss, or FACL, is designed to replace losses such as mean squared error and weighted mean squared error for spatiotemporal signal prediction.

FACL combines two complementary terms. Fourier Amplitude Loss regulates the prediction’s Fourier amplitudes, while Fourier Correlation Loss supplies the phase information the amplitude term misses. The method is described as generic, efficient, and parameter-free. Its focus is on what the model is trained to preserve, rather than on proposing another forecasting architecture.

Experiments on one synthetic dataset and three radar echo datasets improve perceptual measures and meteorological skill scores, with a small trade-off in pixel-wise accuracy and structural similarity. The authors also propose Regional Histogram Divergence, a patch-based similarity measure tolerant of local transformations, to improve the error margin in meteorological scores. The results make the trade-off between different notions of forecast quality explicit.
neurips-2024-fourier-amplitude-and-corre.tldr: FACL improves precipitation forecast perception and meteorological skill through complementary Fourier losses, with small accuracy and structural-similarity trade-offs.

paragraphs: This paper studies how neural networks maintain information about naturalistic objects in working memory. It moves beyond categorical inputs and a small number of tasks by coupling a convolutional network with a recurrent network and training on nine N-back tasks. The analysis examines the recurrent network’s internal representations during task performance.

The trained multitask networks retain both relevant and irrelevant object information. Their organization depends on the recurrent architecture: vanilla RNNs largely share the subspaces for particular object properties across tasks, whereas GRU and LSTM networks use more task-specific subspaces. Object features also become less orthogonal relative to their organization in the perceptual representation.

The authors distinguish the transformation that places an input into memory from those that preserve it through subsequent distractions. The former is shared across stimuli, while retention transformations differ across time. These findings suggest that the trained networks track short-term information through chronologically organized memory subspaces, providing predictions that could be tested against neural data.
neurips-2024-geometry-of-naturalistic-ob.tldr: Networks trained on naturalistic working-memory tasks organize object information in architecture-dependent and time-dependent internal subspaces.

paragraphs: Grid cells are associated with regular spatial firing patterns that support navigation, yet reward-related landmarks can distort those patterns. This paper investigates how spatial coding and reward information interact by training path-integrating recurrent networks to predict position, with particular emphasis on rewarded locations. Grid-like neurons emerge during training.

The authors analyze how rewards alter the resulting population code. They find changes in its geometry while its topology remains preserved: the representation becomes distorted without losing its underlying organization. A striking result is that a local change in reward produces global changes across the grid-like firing patterns.

The findings indicate that the preserved topology supports successful path integration after reward-focused training. At the same time, the resulting diversity of individual neuron responses may encode changing environmental cues. This offers a computational account of how a navigation representation can remain useful for tracking position while being reshaped by the importance of particular locations, with different aspects of the code supporting those roles.
neurips-2024-global-distortions-from-loc.tldr: Reward-focused navigation training globally distorts grid-like neural representations while preserving topology that supports path integration.

paragraphs: HARMONIC addresses the generation of synthetic tables that remain useful while reducing exposure of sensitive source data. Its generation approach uses instruction fine-tuning rather than the continued pretraining used in earlier small-scale LLM methods. The instruction dataset is constructed using an idea based on nearest neighbors to encourage learning relationships between rows.

The intended effect is to teach the model table structure and data relationships rather than individual records, reducing privacy leakage risk. Experiments report comparable utility to existing methods with better privacy under the evaluated measures, including MLE and DCR. These results concern measured privacy improvements, rather than establishing an unconditional privacy guarantee.

The framework also introduces two evaluation measures. DLT quantifies how much information the generator itself leaks, while LLE evaluates performance on downstream LLM tasks. The authors report improvements over previous methods on both. HARMONIC thus treats generation and evaluation together, examining not only whether a synthetic table is useful but also what the generating model may reveal.
neurips-2024-harmonic-harnessing-llms-fo.tldr: HARMONIC uses relationship-focused instruction tuning to generate useful synthetic tables with improved measured privacy.

paragraphs: This paper connects two goals in interactive learning: keeping regret bounded and remaining robust when reward feedback arrives with unknown delays. Prior work identifies a zero Graves-Lai constant as necessary and sufficient for bounded regret. The authors ask whether this restrictive condition also matters for robustness to uncertainty about feedback delays.

They show that it is necessary for a consistent algorithm to achieve delay-model robustness when feedback is anonymous and delays are unknown. Here consistency means uniformly sub-polynomial regret, and robustness is measured using epsilon-robustness. If the Graves-Lai constant is nonzero, such an algorithm cannot achieve that robustness for any positive epsilon, however small.

A positive result applies to linear reward models, including contextual linear bandits and reinforcement learning with a linear MDP. In these settings, a zero constant is also sufficient for bounded regret without knowing the delay model. The results link a condition previously associated with statistical efficiency to robustness, while keeping the sufficiency claim specific to the stated linear settings.
neurips-2024-is-o-log-n-practical-near-e.tldr: A zero Graves-Lai constant is necessary for anonymous-delay robustness and sufficient for delay-agnostic bounded regret in linear reward models.

paragraphs: The examples placed in a vision-language model’s prompt can strongly affect its in-context learning performance. Both which demonstrations are selected and their order matter. Lever-LM treats constructing that sequence as a learning problem, using a small language model to configure demonstrations for a much larger vision-language model.

The approach assumes that effective demonstration sequences contain statistical patterns that a language model can learn, drawing an analogy with composing sentences. The authors construct a dataset of effective sequences and train Lever-LM on it. For a new query, the trained model produces a demonstration sequence to support the larger model’s task.

Experiments evaluate this strategy on visual question answering and image captioning using two large vision-language models. The configured sequences outperform several strong baselines, supporting the hypothesis that useful sequence patterns can be learned. The paper illustrates the size contrast with a 67-million-parameter transformer configuring context for models with 9 billion parameters, making prompt construction the smaller model’s substantive contribution.
neurips-2024-lever-lm-configuring-in-con.tldr: Lever-LM learns to select and order demonstrations that improve larger vision-language models’ in-context performance.

paragraphs: Identification asks whether a causal model’s unknown parameters can be determined from observational data together with assumptions about its graphical structure. For linear structural causal models, the observations are represented by a covariance matrix. This paper studies the computational difficulty of deciding identification, rather than assuming that observational associations uniquely determine causal parameters.

The authors provide a sound and complete algorithm for generic identification that uses polynomial space. A standard complexity result gives an exponential-time simulation, improving substantially on the previous doubly exponential method based on Gröbner bases. This establishes a better computational upper bound for the generic identification problem.

The paper also proves hardness for a distinct question about a given feasible correlation matrix: whether exactly one parameter set, or multiple parameter sets, can explain it. That problem is hard for the universal theory of the reals and, consequently, coNP-hard. Together, the results improve the known algorithmic guarantee while showing that identification still includes computationally hard cases.
neurips-2024-on-the-complexity-of-identi.tldr: A polynomial-space algorithm improves generic causal identification bounds, while a related uniqueness problem is proved computationally hard.

paragraphs: QuaRot makes language models easier to quantize by rotating their internal representations to remove hidden-state outliers. The rotations preserve the model’s output before quantization. This distinction matters: reorganizing the computation does not itself change the answer, while the subsequent reduction in numerical precision can introduce an accuracy loss.

The approach applies this invariance to residual hidden states, feed-forward activations, parts of attention, and the key-value cache. It quantizes weights, activations, and that cache to four bits. All matrix multiplications then operate in four bits, without keeping selected channels at higher precision to accommodate outliers.

For the reported four-bit LLAMA2-70B model, the WikiText-2 perplexity loss is at most 0.47, and the model retains 99% of its zero-shot performance. The authors also demonstrate lossless six- and eight-bit LLAMA-2 models using round-to-nearest quantization without calibration data. The findings show how an output-preserving change of representation can support aggressive precision reduction with small reported losses in the four-bit setting.
neurips-2024-quarot-outlier-free-4-bit-i.tldr: QuaRot removes internal outliers through output-preserving rotations, enabling end-to-end four-bit language-model inference with small reported performance losses.

paragraphs: Influential language-model scaling laws disagree about the model size that best uses a fixed compute budget. This paper investigates why the predictions associated with Kaplan and Hoffmann differ. The authors first reproduce the Kaplan scaling law on OpenWebText2 and RefinedWeb, giving them a basis for examining the source of the discrepancy.

They identify three contributing factors: the computational cost of the last layer, the duration of learning-rate warmup, and optimizer tuning that depends on scale. Correcting these factors produces close agreement with the Hoffmann, or Chinchilla, scaling law. The result connects the disagreement to how computation and training choices are handled.

The study also finds that carefully designed learning-rate decay is not essential for the Chinchilla law to hold, contrary to a proposed explanation. As a secondary contribution, it derives scaling laws for the optimal learning rate and batch size. It further finds that tuning AdamW’s beta-two parameter is essential at lower batch sizes, reinforcing the importance of optimizer choices when comparing training scales.
neurips-2024-resolving-discrepancies-in-.tldr: Compute accounting, warmup duration, and scale-dependent optimizer tuning explain the studied discrepancy between Kaplan and Chinchilla scaling laws.

paragraphs: Estimating the centers of mixture components becomes especially difficult when arbitrary outliers outnumber a genuine small component. The outliers can imitate additional groups, making it impossible to restrict a list of candidate centers to the true number of components while still recovering every true center accurately. The paper calls this setting list-decodable mixture learning.

The proposed algorithm achieves order-optimal error guarantees for each mixture mean with minimal extra list size. It improves substantially over list-decodable mean estimation, the existing method applicable to this setting. The output list accommodates ambiguity introduced by adversarially fabricated groups while retaining accurate candidates for the genuine means.

For separated mixtures, the algorithm uses mixture structure to partially cluster the data, then carefully applies a base list-decodable mean learner at different scales. Its strongest guarantees rely on this separation, although improvements are also observed without separation. The work shows how exploiting relationships among components can improve recovery beyond treating the task solely as repeated robust mean estimation.
neurips-2024-robust-mixture-learning-whe.tldr: A mixture-aware algorithm accurately recovers candidate component means even when adversarial outliers overwhelm small groups.

paragraphs: Boosting combines weak learners into a more accurate predictor. In the realizable setting, its sample requirements can match empirical risk minimization while offering computational advantages. In the agnostic setting, which makes no assumptions about the conditional distribution of labels given features, previously known boosting algorithms have required quadratically more samples than empirical risk minimization.

This paper makes progress toward closing that gap with a substantially more sample-efficient agnostic boosting algorithm. It preserves the computational or oracle complexity of existing approaches. A key ingredient is reusing samples over several boosting rounds, allowing the same observations to support multiple stages of the learning process.

The analysis guarantees a generalization error strictly better than what follows from black-box uniform convergence arguments. Thus, the contribution includes both an algorithmic use of sample reuse and a sharper account of its consequences. The authors also apply the approach to other learning problems, including boosting for reinforcement learning, and obtain improved results. The stated advance narrows the sample-efficiency gap rather than claiming to eliminate it.
neurips-2024-sample-efficient-agnostic-b.tldr: Reusing samples across boosting rounds improves agnostic boosting’s sample efficiency without sacrificing computational complexity.

paragraphs: Streaming Detection of Queried Event Start asks a video system to recognize when an event described in natural language begins. The emphasis is on responding accurately and with little delay as the video unfolds. This task reflects applications such as robotics and augmented reality, where recognizing an event’s onset is important for timely reactions.

The authors introduce a benchmark based on Ego4D and task-specific metrics for this setting. The evaluation covers diverse events in first-person video, combining the need to understand a language query with the need to track an ongoing visual sequence. Accuracy and latency are both part of the intended task.

They also propose adapter-based baselines inspired by parameter-efficient fine-tuning. These methods transfer image-model capabilities to video and support efficient online modeling. The study evaluates three vision-language backbones and three adapter architectures on both short clips and untrimmed videos. Its contribution establishes a task, evaluation resources, and baseline approaches for studying query-driven event onset detection under streaming conditions.
neurips-2024-streaming-detection-of-quer.tldr: SDQES introduces a benchmark and adapter-based baselines for detecting language-described event starts accurately and promptly in streaming video.

paragraphs: SustainDC provides Python environments for studying sustainable data center control with multi-agent reinforcement learning. The motivation is the energy consumption and climate impact associated with growing computational demand. Its focus is a setting where several operational decisions interact, so evaluating each controller independently would miss part of the control problem.

The environments support custom data center configurations and tasks including workload scheduling, cooling optimization, and auxiliary battery management. Multiple agents manage these operations while accounting for one another’s effects. This makes coordinated decision making part of the benchmark rather than treating workload, cooling, and storage as unrelated tasks.

The authors evaluate reinforcement learning algorithms across different data center designs, locations, weather conditions, grid carbon intensities, and workload requirements. Their results highlight substantial opportunities to improve operations using multi-agent methods. SustainDC’s main contribution is a configurable platform for developing and comparing such algorithms across varied operating conditions, with sustainability motivating both the control tasks and the evaluation setting.
neurips-2024-sustaindc-benchmarking-for-.tldr: SustainDC benchmarks coordinated reinforcement learning for workload scheduling, cooling, and battery control across varied data center conditions.

paragraphs: Point cloud recognition models can rely too heavily on particular patterns and become less robust when their inputs are corrupted. APCT addresses this by erasing significant features during training, encouraging the model to capture a broader range of object structure. The features targeted for erasure depend on the patterns identified at each training step.

An Adversarial Significance Identifier estimates token importance using global context, a structural salience index, and auxiliary supervision. A Target-guided Promptor then uses those importance values to increase the tendency to discard tokens within self-attention. This directs later processing toward alternative parts of the object representation.

Repeating the process over multiple training steps encourages the network to identify and integrate additional object-related patterns. The mechanism aims to strengthen global structure capture by making familiar cues less dependable during training. Experiments report state-of-the-art results on multiple corruption benchmarks, supporting this strategy for improving recognition robustness in the evaluated corrupted point cloud settings.
neurips-2024-target-guided-adversarial-p.tldr: APCT repeatedly suppresses important point-cloud features during training to learn broader object structure and improve corruption robustness.
